newsitem.title: CANADA: Wal-Mart Canada loses bid to decertify union.
newsitem.headline: Wal-Mart Canada loses bid to decertify union.

text.p: Wal-Mart Canada Inc, a unit of Wal-Mart Stores Inc, lost its bid to decertify its first union on Thursday when an Ontario court ruled that the retailer breached the law during the union's first organizing campaign, the union said on Thursday.

Wal-Mart had applied for a judicial review of the OLRB's January decision, which ruled that the United Steelworkers of America could represent the 209 employees at Wal-Mart's Windsor, Ontario store even though a majority of the workers voted against unionizing.

The Ontario court upheld the OLRB's decision and concluded that Wal-Mart intimidated workers by refusing to answer their questions about whether the store would remain open if a union were introduced.
The court dismissed Wal-Mart's application for a judicial review, concluding the board did not commit a reviewable error.

"The court's decision upholds the OLRB's finding that Wal-Mart interfered with the employees' free choice," said Dan Garvey, assistant to the Canadian director of Retail Wholesale Canada, the Steelworkers' retail wholesale division.

"Wal-Mart's actions tainted the vote in such a way that instead of asking whether the employees wanted a union, they were being asked if they wanted a job. It's impossible to say that the vote held last May was a true reflection of the workers' wishes," Garvey added.
Wal-Mart could not be reached for comment.
The Windsor store is the first of about 2,600 Wal-mart stores worldwide to be unionized.
Garvey said the union's first priority was to bargain a collective agreement, as the workers remained without a contract.
